classification.difficultyReason: Requires differentiating twice, comparing both sides of the differential equation and checking two initial conditions.

content.prompt: Show that $y=\tan x$ is a solution of the IVP $y''=2yy'$, with $y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1$ and $y'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=2$.

answer.short: $y'=\sec^2 x$ and $y''=2\sec^2 x\tan x=2yy'$. Also, $y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1$ and $y'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=2$, so $y=\tan x$ satisfies the IVP.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y'&=\sec^2 x\\y''&=2\sec^2 x\tan x\end{align*}$$
The right-hand side is
$$\begin{align*}2yy'&=2\tan x\cdot\sec^2 x\\2yy'&=2\sec^2 x\tan x\\2yy'&=y''\end{align*}$$
Check the initial conditions:
$$\begin{align*}y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)&=\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1\\y'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)&=\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=2\end{align*}$$
Therefore $y=\tan x$ is a solution of the IVP.
